claims.source: Lu, Sclar, Hallinan, Mireshghallah, Liu, Han, Ettinger, Jiang, Chandu, Dziri and Choi (UW/AI2), arXiv 2410.04265 v2

claims.claim: Yun et al. attribute a diversity collapse in instruction-tuned LLMs to the structural tokens of the chat template rather than to decoding randomness.
claims.source: Yun, An, Wang, Peng and Shang (UC San Diego), arXiv 2505.18949 v1

claims.claim: Yun et al. found that prompting for diversity inside a chat template still failed to close the gap with a minimal prompt.
claims.source: Yun, An, Wang, Peng and Shang (UC San Diego), arXiv 2505.18949 v1
claims.quote: still fails to close the gap with Simple
claims.page: Section 5.5, Explicit Prompts for Diversity Still Fall Short

claims.claim: Yun et al. report that prompts using full chat templates gain substantially less diversity from temperature scaling than simple steer prompts do.
claims.source: Yun, An, Wang, Peng and Shang (UC San Diego), arXiv 2505.18949 v1
claims.quote: from temperature scaling are substantially smaller
claims.page: Section 5.4, Effect of Decoding Temperature on Diversity

claims.claim: In Yun et al.'s WritingPrompts task the semantic diversity was 0.3291 under the full chat template, 0.4767 under a simple steer prompt and 0.3427 under the template with an explicit diversity instruction.
claims.source: Yun, An, Wang, Peng and Shang (UC San Diego), arXiv 2505.18949 v1

claims.claim: Gerstgrasser et al. demonstrate that accumulating successive generations of synthetic data alongside the original real data avoids model collapse.
claims.source: Gerstgrasser, Schaeffer, Dey, Rafailov et al. (Stanford and others), arXiv 2404.01413
claims.quote: generations of synthetic data alongside the original real data avoids model

claims.claim: Gerstgrasser et al. confirm that replacing the original real data by each generation's synthetic data does tend towards model collapse.
claims.source: Gerstgrasser, Schaeffer, Dey, Rafailov et al. (Stanford and others), arXiv 2404.01413
claims.quote: the original real data by each generation

claims.claim: Shypula et al. find that preference-tuned models exhibit greater effective semantic diversity than SFT or base models once quality thresholds are applied.

claims.quote: duce less semantically diverse content within that subset

claims.claim: Shypula et al. report that for open-ended creative writing preference tuning is linked to greater diversity in lexical patterns.

claims.quote: preference tuning is linked to greater diversity in lexical patterns
